findings.title: HTTPS failure recovery does not restore the complete prior service state
findings.trigger: Repeat HTTPS setup on an active existing HTTPS instance. Inject a one-time daemon-reload error after stop, or a one-time startup error after all four services are stopped.
findings.observed: The daemon-reload error happens before the try block: gateway, worker, Authelia and Caddy all remain stopped while https.json still says phase=active. A startup error reaches recovery, but recovery starts only worker/gateway and leaves both existing edge services stopped.
findings.impact: A failed management operation takes the previously usable HTTPS endpoint offline; the ordinary repair command also only restarts gateway/worker. No durable pre-stop snapshot records the complete old edge/service state.
findings.reproduction: .work/preaudit-deploy-fixture.py: existingHttpsReloadFailure and existingHttpsStartupFailure; local temporary files and mocked system operations only
findings.recommendation: Persist the complete pre-stop configuration and intended prior service state, include every destructive step in the transaction, and restore/verify the previously active edge and identity services after confirmed stop. Retain recovery state if stop or restoration cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Existing provided-TLS setup silently ignores newly supplied certificate material
findings.trigger: After installing provided TLS, invoke https again with the same hosts/options and a new --certificate/--private-key pair, as for certificate renewal.
findings.observed: The operation returns success without calling read_pem for either supplied path. The old certificate bytes and hashes remain selected.
findings.impact: A certificate renewal attempt appears successful but continues serving the old, potentially expired certificate.
findings.reproduction: .work/preaudit-deploy-fixture.py: providedCertificateRenewal reports success=true, pemReadCount=0 and retainedCertificate='old certificate'
findings.recommendation: Either perform an explicit validated certificate transaction or reject changed supplied material before stopping services; do not silently discard accepted CLI inputs.

findings.title: Documented authentication-port option is not accepted by the CLI
findings.observed: argparse exits 2 with 'unrecognized arguments: --auth-port 19091'; the actual flag is --authelia-port.
findings.impact: The documented independent-port HTTPS command cannot be run as written.
findings.recommendation: Use the actual --authelia-port option in the guide or deliberately add the documented alias.
